images.caption: Figure 2:Proposal tree construction.① We randomly sample anchors from a reference response and extract target context features. ② The current drafter samples continuations in parallel at these anchors, conditioned on their respective reference contexts. ③ We attach the sampled continuations to their anchors, forming a tree with a shared reference trunk and separate draft branches. Branch independence enables parallel collection, while shared ancestors expose reusable target computation.

Figure 3:Branch-parallel scoring with full attention ().The tree attention mask lets packed queries share trunk KV while restricting each row to itself and its ancestors. Rows and columns follow the same packed-token order. Blue arrows connect each anchor to all query rows in its draft branch;Promptaggregates the shared prompt prefix. Terminal sampleswalkandmusicuse predecessor readouts and need no query rows.

Figure 4:Branch-parallel scoring with sparse attention ().Left-hand tokens are predicted from the predecessor queries named in the right-hand rows. ① All rows reuse complete trunk group keys, including the group ending atEnjoy. Incomplete boundary groups remain in the causal tail. For the branch atevening, predictingwithuses the query ateveningand reads[a, quiet, evening]as a 3/4 causal tail; predictingsoftuses the query atwith, which completes[a, quiet, evening, with](4/4) and requires a branch-specific indexer group key. Anchor and bell icons mark branch points and rebuilding. ② Indexer queries select eligible complete groups with top-kk; attention reads selected KV plus the causal tail, which bypasses top-kk.

Figure 5:Branch-parallel scoring with linear attention ().A shared trunk pass caches anFP32GDN state afterEnjoyat theC=64C=64boundary (63 prompt tokens omitted). In the indexed recurrent kernel, each thread block (CTA) loads its state tile from this checkpoint into private registers (Copy State).Replay Tokensuses cached trunk features to advance it throughaora→\toquiet→\toevening, restoring the anchor state.Update Statethen processes branch tokens, updating the state and reading it with each token’s query to produce GDN outputs. Checkpoints remain immutable; causal convolution follows branch ancestry.
